content_html:
A wasp nest near a doorway, play area, or busy path can create a sting risk, but approaching it, striking it, or spraying from a ladder increases that risk. The right response depends on species, nest location, nest size, and whether anyone nearby has a severe sting allergy.

Keep your distance and reroute foot traffic

Do not block the nest entrance or stand close to it to watch activity. Keep children and pets away and use another doorway or path while deciding what to do next.

High, concealed, or very active nests are not ladder jobs

Treating a nest from a ladder combines sting risk with fall risk. Nests high under eaves, inside wall cavities, chimneys, or other locations without safe access are appropriate for a pest-management professional.

Factor in sting allergies and occupied areas

If anyone has a history of severe sting reactions, minimize exposure and do not turn nest removal into a home experiment. A nest beside a main entrance or children’s area deserves a lower threshold for professional service.

Do not seal an active entry before the nest is resolved

Sealing an opening while wasps are still active inside can drive them toward another exit, including into the home. Exclusion comes after the nest is inactive or removed and activity at the opening has stopped.
